headline: The Prime Minister announces the first national lockdown
detail: Announced on the evening of 23 March; the measures became law three days later.
quote: PM announces the first lockdown in the UK, ordering people to “stay at home”
notes: The counterpart for five UCL rows, and the anchor of the lag analysis in both directions. UCL had already stopped face-to-face teaching ten days earlier and barred staff from campus the day after this.

headline: The first lockdown measures come into force
detail: Three days after the announcement.
quote: Lockdown measures legally come into force
notes: The gap between announcement and legal force is why the ledger separates announced from effective dates.

headline: The Prime Minister announces a conditional plan for lifting the lockdown
detail: The first easing of the first lockdown, including a return to the workplace for those who could not work from home.
quote: PM announces a conditional plan for lifting lockdown, and says that people who cannot work from home should return to the workplace but avoid public transport
notes: UCL diverged from this the next day, asking staff not to return to campus. That is the clearest case in the record of UCL declining an easing rather than following one.

headline: Schools in England begin a phased reopening
detail: The date UCL aligned its first campus reopening pilots with.
quote: Phased re-opening of schools in England
notes: UCL said on 26 May that it had aligned its pilot activity with the proposed dates for schools to return, which makes this a dependency of a UCL timetable on a national schools decision.

headline: The Prime Minister announces a relaxing of the 2 metre distancing rule
detail: The move that became the "1 metre plus" guidance, taking effect with the wider easing of 4 July.
quote: PM says UK’s “national hibernation” coming to an end – announces relaxing of restrictions and 2m social distancing rule
notes: The source records a relaxing of the 2 metre rule and does not use the phrase "one metre plus"; the headline follows the source rather than UCL's wording for it. UCL kept 2 metres for Term 1 timetable planning, which is the sharpest deliberate divergence in the whole record.

headline: Face coverings become mandatory on public transport in England
detail: The Health Protection (Coronavirus, Wearing of Face Coverings on Public Transport) (England) Regulations 2020, SI 2020/592.
quote: These Regulations come into force on 15th June 2020
notes: UCL had required face coverings on campus where distancing was not possible from 22 May, twenty-four days before this. The date was carried for a while on a UCL newsletter's authority and then withdrawn, because reference 7 gives 15 June as the day non-essential shops reopened and says nothing about transport. Both are true of that day; the regulations are what establish the second.

headline: The Plan B face covering requirement in England expires
detail: SI 2021/1400 amends regulation 15 of the Plan B face covering regulations, substituting 26th January 2022 for 20th December 2021, so the requirement lapses at the end of that day.
quote: They also extend the period during which the Regulations are in force until 26th January 2022
notes: UCL kept face coverings mandatory on the day the legal requirement ended and narrowed them to teaching settings twenty-six days later. This is the second time the record shows UCL holding a measure after the law dropped it, the first being step 4 in July 2021.

headline: The first local lockdown is announced for Leicester
detail: Announced by the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care.
quote: Matt Hancock announces that the UK’s first local lockdown would be applied in Leicester and parts of Leicestershire
notes: UCL cited this on 8 July as a reason for caution in its own planning.

headline: The first local lockdown comes into force in Leicester
detail: The same day as the wider easing in the rest of England.
quote: UK’s first local lockdown comes into force in Leicester and parts of Leicestershire. More restrictions are eased in England, including reopening of pubs, restaurants, hairdressers.
notes: The two limbs of this entry are why 4 July is the phase boundary in this chronology: England eased and one city did not.

headline: The rule of six bans social gatherings above six in England
detail: Applied indoors and outdoors.
quote: ‘Rule of six’ – indoor and outdoor social gatherings above six banned in England
notes: UCL noted it on 9 September while saying it had not yet decided what to do, which is rare candour in the record.

headline: A three-tier system of restrictions starts in England
detail: London moved to Tier 2 on 17 October and UCL stayed open.
quote: A new three-tier system of Covid-19 restrictions starts in England
notes: The tier system is the mechanism by which national policy reached UCL geographically rather than sectorally.

headline: The Prime Minister announces a second national lockdown for England
detail: Announced on a Saturday; the measures came into force on 5 November.
quote: PM announces a second lockdown in England to prevent a “medical and moral disaster” for the NHS
notes: This source does not say that universities were to stay open. That is UCL's account of the policy, recorded in the UCL row of 1 November, and it still needs a primary source of its own. The distinction matters because the exemption is the reason the case series behaves differently in the two lockdowns.

headline: The second national lockdown comes into force in England
detail: A four-week closure of non-essential retail, with educational settings treated differently from the first lockdown.
quote: Second national lockdown comes into force in England

headline: The Department for Education publishes Christmas travel guidance for students
detail: Published by the Department for Education and the Minister of State for Universities.
quote: University students will be able to travel home to spend Christmas with their families once the national restrictions end on 2 December, following steps set out in new Government guidance published today.
notes: The sector-specific counterpart to the second lockdown, and the reason UCL restricted travel to essential journeys until 2 December.

headline: The second lockdown ends and England returns to the tier system
detail: London returned to Tier 2.
quote: Second lockdown ends after four weeks and England returns to a stricter three-tier system of restrictions

headline: The student travel window opens
detail: A six-day window with staggered departure dates set by each university.
quote: From 3 December to 9 December, which will be known as the ‘student travel window’, students will be allowed to travel home on staggered departure dates set by universities, who will work with other institutions in the region to manage pressure on transport infrastructure.
notes: A national policy written specifically for universities, and one of the few that treats the student population as an epidemiological object in its own right.

headline: Tier 4 announced for London and the South East
detail: A new "Stay at Home" alert level, with the planned Christmas relaxation cut short.
quote: PM announces tougher restrictions for London and South East England, with a new Tier 4: ‘Stay at Home’ alert level. Christmas mixing rules tightened.
notes: The start of the phase in which UCL's January 2021 rise occurs. Attributing that rise to the Alpha variant is an epidemiological claim none of the cached sources makes, so it is not made here: what the ledger supports is that the restrictions tightened and the figures rose.

headline: England enters the third national lockdown
detail: Announced by the Prime Minister on the evening of 4 January and in force from 6 January.
quote: England enters third national lockdown
notes: UCL responded on 5 January, between the announcement and the legal commencement. The ledger dates this row to the date this source gives, which is the commencement.

headline: The government publishes the roadmap out of lockdown
detail: Four steps, replacing the regional tier system with uniform national easing.
quote: PM publishes a roadmap for lifting the lockdown
notes: UCL published its own roadmap tracking these four steps on 23 March 2021.

headline: Step 4 of the roadmap delayed by four weeks to 19 July
detail: Delayed in response to the Delta variant.
quote: delayed by four weeks, until 19 July, as the government accelerates the vaccination programme.
notes: UCL's return timetable slipped with it, which is the clearest case in the record of a UCL date moving purely because a national date moved.

headline: Step 4 removes most legal limits on social contact in England
detail: The end of the legal requirements, including distancing and face coverings.
quote: Most legal limits on social contact removed
notes: UCL kept face coverings in all indoor spaces a week later, and this ends the 2 metre rule UCL had held since 8 July 2020.

headline: The government announces a move to Plan B measures in England
detail: Guidance to work from home, with face coverings and the NHS Covid Pass.
quote: PM announces a move to ‘Plan B’ measures in England following the spread of the Omicron variant.
notes: This source does not record the higher education exemption. That is UCL's account, and it is the reason UCL stayed open through the highest case counts in the whole series.

headline: Face masks become compulsory in most indoor venues under Plan B
quote: Face masks become compulsory in most public indoor venues under Plan B.
notes: UCL had made face coverings mandatory indoors on campus on 30 November, ten days ahead of this.
